notes: All seven web searches ran this time (six required plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act). None returned anything by Rep. Craig A. Goldman (R-TX) on AI; results for his name were about other people (Dr. Craig A. Kaplan, Goldman Sachs) or other members. The site-restricted search returned no pages from craiggoldman.house.gov. From the earlier run (kept): his official press release pages were opened directly (https://craiggoldman.house.gov/media/press-releases and ?page=1, 20 releases from 20 March 2025 to 26 October 2026) and none mentions artificial intelligence according to the page-reading tool's summaries (releases were not each opened individually); his 22 April 2026 data privacy bill release (https://craiggoldman.house.gov/media/press-releases/rep-goldman-introduction-data-privacy-bill) does not mention AI in his quoted words. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, introduced 24 September 2026): the fastdemocracy.com bill page (https://fastdemocracy.com/bill-search/us/119/bills/USB00108512/) lists 12 cosponsors, all Democrats, and he is not among them; congress.gov returned an access error so the official list was not checked. One search result was a 18 September 2025 House Judiciary AI hearing transcript (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CHRG-119hhrg61690/html/CHRG-119hhrg61690.htm); on opening it (first 100,000 of 126,002 characters read), the only Goldman is Daniel S. Goldman of New York, with no remarks by Craig Goldman. He sits on the Energy and Commerce Committee, which handles AI legislation, so committee hearing transcripts not indexed by search could still contain AI remarks. No House letter about AI risk signed by him was found. Not to be confused with Rep. Daniel Goldman (New York).
